summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: polaprezinc as an adjunct to H. pylori triple therapy raises eradication rates (RCT +17-18 points; meta-analysis OR 2.01, very low quality). Full texts confirm polaprezinc raises H. pylori eradication when added to triple therapy (RCT +17-18 points; meta-analysis ITT OR 2.01, very low quality) and gives no significant between-group benefit in a 20-patient aspirin-injury pilot. The other two sources are a comparator ulcer trial (abstract only) and a rectal-enema colitis trial. These are drug-adjunct settings, and Dr. Pham rejected generic gut-barrier approval, so none supports the record's retail Digestive/Immune claim. The record becomes reference-only, which removes zinc-carnosine Evidence points from dependent products (about 2 per the closure plan).

identity.preparation: Polaprezinc zinc-L-carnosine complex added to triple therapy; not elemental zinc alone.

population.description: Adults with H. pylori-associated gastritis at multiple Chinese centres randomized 1:1:1 to polaprezinc 150 mg/d or 300 mg/d plus clarithromycin triple therapy, or triple therapy alone (ITT arms 107, 99, 103 for safety).

study_contexts.study_design: Prospective, randomized, parallel-group, open-label, controlled multicentre trial; primary endpoint H. pylori eradication 4 weeks after treatment by urea breath test.

outcomes.name: Primary H. pylori eradication (ITT): 77.0% (150 mg/d) and 75.9% (300 mg/d) vs 58.6% triple therapy alone; +18.4% (95% CI 6.4-30.4) and +17.4% (5.2-29.6), P<0.01; no difference between doses (P=0.90).
Higher-dose adverse-event frequency exceeded standard dose and control; no universal safety equivalence.

limitations: Open-label adjunctive treatment; no generic gut-barrier or standalone eradication approval.
Dose is total polaprezinc complex, not elemental zinc; do not invent component allocations.
Returned decision: Reject generic “gut barrier” approval; source-content hold for specific adjunctive settings.
